name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q01 - Sequence of major metallurgical steps

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following major steps involved in the extraction and isolation of a metal from its mined ore in the correct chronological sequence:

  1. Isolation of the crude metal from its concentrated ore
  2. Grading and crushing of the mined ore to a reasonable size
  3. Purification (refining) of the crude metal
  4. Concentration (benefaction) of the ore to remove gangue

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Metallurgy follows a logical progression from preparing the raw mined ore, removing earthly impurities, chemically isolating the crude metal, and finally purifying it to high purity.

Step 2: Ordering the Stages
First, the mined ore is graded and crushed to a reasonable particle size. Next, unwanted gangue materials are removed by concentration (dressing or benefaction). After concentration, the concentrated ore is converted to a suitable form (usually oxide) and reduced to isolate the crude metal. Finally, the crude metal is purified by refining techniques.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological sequence is grading and crushing of the mined ore, followed by concentration (benefaction), then isolation of the crude metal, and finally purification (refining) of the crude metal.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q02 - Sequence of leaching alumina from bauxite

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following steps in the correct sequence for obtaining pure \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) from bauxite ore by leaching:

  1. Neutralisation of sodium aluminate solution with \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) gas and seeding with freshly prepared hydrated \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\)
  2. Filtration, drying, and heating of hydrated alumina at \(1470\,\mathrm{K}\) to obtain pure \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\)
  3. Digestion of powdered bauxite with concentrated \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) at \(473\text{--}523\,\mathrm{K}\) and \(35\text{--}36\,\mathrm{bar}\)
  4. Precipitation of hydrated \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3 \cdot xH_2O}\) while sodium silicate remains in solution

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Alumina is separated from \(\mathrm{SiO_2}\), iron oxides, and \(\mathrm{TiO_2}\) impurities in bauxite through selective dissolution (digestion), precipitation, and thermal dehydration.

Step 2: Ordering the Stages
First, powdered bauxite undergoes digestion with concentrated \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) at \(473\text{--}523\,\mathrm{K}\) and \(35\text{--}36\,\mathrm{bar}\) to form soluble sodium aluminate (and sodium silicate). Second, the sodium aluminate solution is neutralised by passing \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) gas and seeded with freshly prepared hydrated \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\). Third, hydrated alumina (\(\mathrm{Al_2O_3 \cdot xH_2O}\)) precipitates out while sodium silicate stays dissolved. Fourth, the precipitate is filtered, dried, and heated at \(1470\,\mathrm{K}\) to yield pure \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence is digestion with \(\mathrm{NaOH}\), followed by neutralisation with \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and seeding, then precipitation of hydrated alumina, and finally filtration, drying, and heating at \(1470\,\mathrm{K}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q03 - Sequence of blister copper production

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following stages in the extraction of blister copper from an iron-containing copper sulphide ore in the correct chronological sequence:

  1. Self-reduction of \(\mathrm{Cu_2O}\) with \(\mathrm{Cu_2S}\) via \(2\mathrm{Cu_2O} + \mathrm{Cu_2S} \rightarrow 6\mathrm{Cu} + \mathrm{SO_2}\)
  2. Heating the ore with silica in a reverberatory furnace to slag off iron oxide as \(\mathrm{FeSiO_3}\) and produce copper matte
  3. Charging copper matte into a silica-lined converter and blowing a hot air blast to oxidise remaining \(\mathrm{FeS}\) and \(\mathrm{Cu_2S}\)
  4. Solidification of molten copper accompanied by evolution of \(\mathrm{SO_2}\) gas

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Copper extraction from iron-bearing sulphide ores proceeds by smelting to remove iron as slag and obtain copper matte, followed by conversion in a silica-lined converter.

Step 2: Ordering the Stages
First, the ore is mixed with silica and heated in a reverberatory furnace so iron oxide forms \(\mathrm{FeSiO_3}\) slag and copper is obtained as copper matte (\(\mathrm{Cu_2S}\) and \(\mathrm{FeS}\)). Second, the copper matte is charged into a silica-lined converter with some silica, and a hot air blast oxidises the remaining \(\mathrm{FeS}\) (slagged off) and partially oxidises \(\mathrm{Cu_2S}\) to \(\mathrm{Cu_2O}\). Third, self-reduction takes place between \(\mathrm{Cu_2O}\) and \(\mathrm{Cu_2S}\) to form molten metallic copper and \(\mathrm{SO_2}\). Fourth, as the molten copper solidifies, escaping \(\mathrm{SO_2}\) gas gives it a blistered appearance (blister copper).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence is reverberatory furnace smelting to copper matte, charging into a silica-lined converter with hot air blast, self-reduction of \(\mathrm{Cu_2O}\) with \(\mathrm{Cu_2S}\), and solidification with \(\mathrm{SO_2}\) evolution.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q04 - Sequence of gold extraction by cyanide leaching

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following steps in the extraction of gold using cyanide leaching in the correct chronological sequence:

  1. Addition of solid zinc to act as a reducing agent
  2. Treatment of the gold-bearing material with dilute \(\mathrm{NaCN}\) solution in the presence of air (\(\mathrm{O_2}\))
  3. Formation of soluble dicyanoaurate(I) complex \([\mathrm{Au(CN)_2}]^-\) in aqueous solution
  4. Precipitation of metallic gold along with formation of \([\mathrm{Zn(CN)_4}]^{2-}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Gold is extracted by hydrometallurgical leaching involving oxidation to a soluble cyanide complex, followed by reductive displacement using zinc.

Step 2: Ordering the Stages
First, the gold-bearing material is leached with dilute \(\mathrm{NaCN}\) (or \(\mathrm{KCN}\)) in the presence of air supplying \(\mathrm{O_2}\). Second, gold is oxidised and dissolves as the soluble complex \([\mathrm{Au(CN)_2}]^-\) according to \(4\mathrm{Au} + 8\mathrm{CN}^- + 2\mathrm{H_2O} + \mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow 4[\mathrm{Au(CN)_2}]^- + 4\mathrm{OH}^-\). Third, solid zinc is added to the solution as a reducing agent. Fourth, zinc displaces gold from the complex, precipitating metallic gold and forming \([\mathrm{Zn(CN)_4}]^{2-}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence is treatment with dilute \(\mathrm{NaCN}\) and air, formation of soluble \([\mathrm{Au(CN)_2}]^-\), addition of solid zinc, and precipitation of metallic gold with \([\mathrm{Zn(CN)_4}]^{2-}\) formation.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q05 - Sequence from pig iron to wrought iron

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following steps in the production of wrought iron starting from iron ore in the correct chronological sequence:

  1. Melting pig iron with scrap iron and coke using a hot air blast to obtain cast iron
  2. Reduction of iron oxide ore in a blast furnace to obtain molten pig iron (about \(4\%\) carbon)
  3. Removing the metal and freeing it from slag by passing through rollers to obtain wrought iron
  4. Oxidising impurities in cast iron in a reverberatory furnace lined with haematite and limestone flux

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Commercial iron is refined progressively from pig iron (highest carbon and impurity content) to cast iron and finally to wrought iron (purest commercial form).

Step 2: Ordering the Stages
First, iron oxide ore is reduced in the blast furnace to produce molten pig iron containing about \(4\%\) carbon. Second, pig iron is melted with scrap iron and coke using a hot air blast to produce cast iron (about \(3\%\) carbon). Third, cast iron is heated in a reverberatory furnace lined with haematite (which oxidises carbon to \(\mathrm{CO}\)) and limestone flux (which removes oxidised \(\mathrm{S}\), \(\mathrm{Si}\), and \(\mathrm{P}\) into slag). Fourth, the purified metal is removed and freed from slag by passing through rollers to yield wrought iron.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence is blast furnace reduction to pig iron, melting with scrap iron and coke to cast iron, oxidation of impurities in a haematite-lined reverberatory furnace, and rolling to remove slag and obtain wrought iron.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q06 - Sequence of blast furnace events from top to bottom

questiontext.text:
As iron ore (\(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}\)), limestone, and coke descend from the top to the bottom of a blast furnace, arrange the following events in the order of increasing temperature (top to bottom):

  1. Direct reduction of \(\mathrm{FeO}\) by solid coke (\(\mathrm{FeO} + \mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe} + \mathrm{CO}\)) in the lower high-temperature zone
  2. Stepwise reduction of \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}\) to \(\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}\) by \(\mathrm{CO}\) at \(500\text{--}800\,\mathrm{K}\)
  3. Reduction of \(\mathrm{FeO}\) by \(\mathrm{CO}\) and slag formation (\(\mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{SiO_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CaSiO_3}\)) at \(900\text{--}1500\,\mathrm{K}\)
  4. Collection of molten pig iron at the bottom hearth near \(2170\,\mathrm{K}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In a blast furnace, temperature increases from the top (\(500\text{--}800\,\mathrm{K}\)) toward the bottom tuyeres (up to \(2170\text{--}2200\,\mathrm{K}\)) where coke burns in hot air.

Step 2: Ordering by Temperature
At the top (\(500\text{--}800\,\mathrm{K}\)), rising \(\mathrm{CO}\) first reduces \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}\) to \(\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}\). Further down in the \(900\text{--}1500\,\mathrm{K}\) zone, \(\mathrm{FeO}\) is reduced by \(\mathrm{CO}\) and \(\mathrm{CaO}\) reacts with \(\mathrm{SiO_2}\) to form \(\mathrm{CaSiO_3}\) slag. In the hotter lower zone above \(1073\,\mathrm{K}\) near the burning coke, solid carbon directly reduces \(\mathrm{FeO}\) to \(\mathrm{Fe}\) and \(\mathrm{CO}\). Finally, at the bottom hearth near \(2170\,\mathrm{K}\), molten pig iron collects beneath the molten slag.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct top-to-bottom sequence is reduction of \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}\) to \(\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}\) at \(500\text{--}800\,\mathrm{K}\), reduction of \(\mathrm{FeO}\) by \(\mathrm{CO}\) and slag formation at \(900\text{--}1500\,\mathrm{K}\), direct reduction of \(\mathrm{FeO}\) by coke in the lower high-temperature zone, and collection of molten pig iron near \(2170\,\mathrm{K}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT6_Q07 - Ordering metal oxides by reduction difficulty with carbon

questiontext.text:
Based on their relative vertical positions in the Ellingham diagram (\(\Delta_{\mathrm{r}}G^{\ominus}\) versus \(T\)), arrange the following metal oxides in the increasing order of minimum temperature required for their reduction by carbon (from easiest to hardest to reduce):

  1. \(\mathrm{ZnO}\)
  2. \(\mathrm{Cu_2O}\)
  3. \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\)
  4. \(\mathrm{FeO}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In an Ellingham diagram, oxides whose formation curves lie higher (less negative \(\Delta_{\mathrm{r}}G^{\ominus}\)) are less stable and intersect the downward-sloping \(\mathrm{C, CO}\) line at lower temperatures, making them easier to reduce with carbon.

Step 2: Ordering the Oxides
From top to bottom in the Ellingham diagram: \(\mathrm{Cu_2O}\) lies near the top and is easily reduced by coke at \(500\text{--}600\,\mathrm{K}\); \(\mathrm{FeO}\) lies below \(\mathrm{Cu_2O}\) and is reduced by coke above \(1073\,\mathrm{K}\); \(\mathrm{ZnO}\) lies lower still and requires about \(1673\,\mathrm{K}\) for reduction by coke; \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) lies very low (highly negative \(\Delta_{\mathrm{r}}G^{\ominus}\)) and cannot be economically reduced by carbon in practice, requiring electrolytic reduction instead.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The increasing order of minimum temperature (easiest to hardest to reduce by carbon) is \(\mathrm{Cu_2O}\), then \(\mathrm{FeO}\), then \(\mathrm{ZnO}\), and finally \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\).
